trigger: before POSTing to /remote/postcard/ on a Meural that a bridge is actively pushing to
when Meural postcard POSTs hang with curl rc=000/100 and the bridge logs climbing RENDER_FAILED consecutive failures

claim: MediaManager.checkForMissingMedia (MediaManager.java:965-1068) is a one-item-per-call cursor walk (persistent lastExistChecked advanced before any expansion work), and an empty collection at order 0 is cleanly skipped — it does not abort processing of later collections, and the fetch helpers (LoadFromFile/Factory/getMediaList) return null rather than throw on cold cache.

before trusting func_5f18728a5a96's claim that MediaList.LoadFromFile throws on cold cache

claim: D:\Media\motion\v2 on abydos leaks disk (95GB/95k files) because Media.TryFinalizeJob COPIES worker output to the ArtData serve path and never deletes the motion/v2 copy — every successful crop leaks one file — plus orphaned source copies from jobs that never reached a terminal outcome; stargate-hosted NimbusJobs cannot reap it because motion/v2 is abydos-local.

before designing a motion/v2 cleanup — the reaper must run abydos-local (TryFinalizeJob or the Python worker), not in NimbusJobs on stargate

claim: The 430694 video poison-pill was fixed by jobs-team commit bb21d15 (pi-fhd maxrate 4M→3M, output 25.96 MiB under the locked 30 MiB ceiling), and quarantined media must NOT be bulk re-enqueued afterward because frames self-heal via isContentAvailable re-submitting on the next request; VideoProduction.Status stays 'Invoke' until a frame-request finalize, so judge worker health from D:\nimbus\video-worker\logs\service_stderr.log, not the DB Invoke count, and abydos log timestamps are UTC-7.

claim: The ffmpeg transcode profile for a video crop is resolved per frame product (Media.cs isContentAvailable ~line 482 maps productId to videoProfile), so the same media renders under different profiles per frame — bb21d15's pi-fhd-only maxrate fix left frame 617 (product 21 → profile 'meural' id=3) still busting the 30 MiB ceiling — and any bitrate-ceiling fix must cover every profile that can hit it.
trigger: before shipping a per-profile transcode parameter fix — enumerate every profile that can hit the output ceiling
when the same media transcodes successfully for one frame but fails the size ceiling for another

claim: Because the video crop profile resolves per frame product, static per-profile bitrate cuts are whack-a-mole; the general fix (commit 04ec112, _effective_vbv_kbps) clamps any profile's maxrate down to a duration-derived byte budget so single-pass output fits WORKER_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES regardless of profile or length, paired with NonRetryableJobError and the ba2d954 'retryable' result flag.
trigger: when a worker output-size constraint is violated across multiple frame products/profiles
before adding another static per-profile maxrate tweak to fix a ceiling violation

claim: Do not escalate a 're-incident' from a stale Loki error-log window — confirm live process and queue state (worker pid alive, pending-job count) first, because zero recent CopyComplete rows can mean the worker is idle, not hung.
trigger: before recommending mitigation or a deploy for a suspected worker re-stall based on log tails

claim: Commit b50cb6fe (deployed abydos 2026-07-01) adds server-side poison-media handling: permanent crop failures (retryable===false or ceiling-string match) set VideoProduction.Status='DeadLetter' and isContentAvailable suppresses re-render for 24h, a greppable POISON_MEDIA log.Error token enables Loki alerting, and CopyProducedOutputToBlob retries file-lock IOExceptions 4x with backoff; transient failures like Timeout still self-heal.

before treating a repeated crop resubmit as unbounded — 24h dead-letter suppression may already apply

claim: NimbusService's recurring ~hourly restarts are caused by Nimbus.MaintenanceTask() (picFrameServiceLibrary/Nimbus.cs:249) throwing unhandled empty-sequence/ArgumentNull LINQ exceptions that shut the whole service down — each crash forces an ~80s whole-fleet disconnect and reconnection storm — so rule this out before attributing instability to the deferred x64/LAA memory work.

claim: The v26 power-toggle fix v1 (commit 3df21fd7) is flawed because FrameDetailsWrapper.FlushDebounce() only publishes if a debounce timer is pending, so its 'prompt-publishing' log is a false positive and /status still lags; the correct fix is an unconditional public PublishStatusNow() — a NimbusCommon edit requiring a FULL deploy — and deploy.sh ovh's incremental msbuild can ship a stale DLL, so clean-rebuild and verify the deployed DLL size.
trigger: before relying on FlushDebounce() to force a /status publish

claim: The 2026-07-01 frame↔server desync was MqttHelper's publish path saturating — a single shared IMqttClient with a 30s operation timeout logging ~900 publish timeouts per 60s so retained /status froze fleet-wide — while Redis stayed fresh via Frame.AddOnlineFrame's ~10s direct write; also, the repo App.config MQTT broker values are stale dead-Azure IPs, so read deployed config from C:\NimbusService\NimbusService.exe.config.

when checking deployed MQTT broker config — never trust the repo App.config

claim: Restarting the Nimbus service does not fix the MQTT publish collapse — it re-saturates within ~2 minutes because the single shared QoS1 client's circuit breaker trips on accumulated in-flight PUBACKs and clean-session-disconnects — and the admin web live view fails for the same reason since its SignalR feed comes from MqttStatusHandler subscribing to frame/+/status; QoS0 for high-frequency telemetry was proposed as the likely fix.
trigger: before restarting NimbusService to fix frozen MQTT /status — expect re-saturation within minutes
when the admin web frame view stops live-updating but a manual page reload shows current state

claim: The real MQTT /status loss is circuit-breaker trips — in-flight PUBACKs climb to the 10000 threshold and the clean-session disconnect drops ~394 broker-buffered publishes per trip — while the ~900-1200/min publish-timeout counter is a known benign false positive under ThreadPool load; the loss is intermittent, not continuous, and the root fix is server-team's async TCP handler (backlog_fbfaa7381046).
trigger: when interpreting MqttHelper 'publish timeouts in last 60s' counts — treat as broker-slow, not lost, and look for circuit-breaker trip log lines instead

claim: As interim mitigation for the MqttHelper circuit breaker dropping legacy /status, an optional qos parameter was added to MqttHelper.PublishAsync and FrameDetailsWrapper's /status and both /changed publishes were wired to QoS0 — no PUBACK means in-flight never accumulates so the breaker never trips — v27-safe because PublishFrameStatusAsync already skips v27/MeuralBridge frames (built on master, Tom-gated, not yet deployed at time of writing).
trigger: when evaluating why legacy /status and /changed publish at QoS0 while frame commands stay QoS1

claim: In-place playlist edits (syncAmount or content changes that bump PlayList.Version under the same PlayListId) never reach frames because active-playlist reload is entirely server-push-driven — the server only pushes ChangePlayList on assignment changes, the retained frame config carries no version, and pushes carry version=0 — so frame 602 kept running v6/20s dwell while the DB had v8/1800s.
trigger: when a customer edits a playlist's interval or content and the frame keeps the old behavior
when checking a frame's applied playlist version — grep its picFrame.log for 'Getting media from list:<id> version:'

claim: v27 frames never reloaded on in-place playlist edits because Changes.PlayListContentsChange (Changes.cs:139) was the only sibling change-type writing the Changes row without firing a v27 MQTT push; the built fix pushes JSONCommand Set{playlist,version} to every frame carrying the playlist and setFramePlayList now includes the version key, with open questions on whether the frame reads KeyValues['version'] and whether it reloads on any Set push or only on version mismatch.
trigger: when in-place playlist edits still don't reach v27 frames after the PlayListContentsChange push fix — check the frame's handling of the KeyValues version key

claim: Any new field added to an MQTT frame command must go inside KeyValues (jsc.addKeyValue), never as a top-level JSONCommand property: v26 frames consume frame/+/commands via NimbusService's decode→encode normalizing bridge that re-emits only {cmd, KeyValues}, and a strict-Jackson v26 frame silently drops the whole command on an unknown top-level field.
trigger: before adding a new field to a frame/{uuid}/commands MQTT message

claim: The QoS0 deploy (commits f48fccee+f3b7bc61, 2026-07-01 21:52Z) eliminated circuit-breaker trips and disconnect drops but did NOT restore live /status delivery — the fleet's retained frame/+/status stayed frozen ~20 minutes post-deploy because MQTT send throughput remains starved, leaving the async TCP handler (backlog_fbfaa7381046) as the required root fix.
trigger: when verifying an MQTT fix post-deploy — check that retained /status lastSeen keeps advancing, not just that breaker trips stopped

claim: Frame 616's 'two images at a time' is the Meural native-gallery leak — firmware-baked preloaded galleries (e.g. Hilma af Klint) flash in the swap gap between pushed postcards — confirmed by the customer, and they cannot be removed by the Meural app, a factory reset, or a reboot; the workaround is a solid black image as the only item in the active native gallery with slideshow off.

trigger: before sending {cmd:'Shell'} to a bridge — use the Meural frame uuid and subscribe frame/<uuid>/replies first

claim: 'Web updates but mobile never' happens because web reads Redis (written directly by the FrameDetailsWrapper debounce callback) while mobile reads MQTT /status published in the same callback — and after every NimbusService restart the ~200-frame reconnect storm stalls MqttHelper publishes ('Published' log = enqueued only, then ~888 30s-timeouts/min) so /status never egresses for 14+ minutes, initially attributed to ThreadPool starvation.
trigger: when frame state changes reach the web UI but never the mobile app after a NimbusService restart

claim: Correcting learning_72c94041dd6bfad6: the post-restart /status publish stall is in the MQTT shared-client connection/send pipeline, not ThreadPool starvation — backlog_a4f6a467a290 measured the :36004 accept-path pool as 30x over-provisioned, and MqttHelper.PublishAsync simply loses its 30s Task.WhenAny race when the single shared publisher connection is stalled — so the fix axis is MQTT client connection health, not ThreadPool decoupling.
trigger: before attributing the post-restart /status stall to ThreadPool starvation

claim: The code-grounded /status stall mechanism: MqttHelper wraps one raw IMqttClient with no publish queue, EnsureConnectedAsync serializes every disconnected-state publish behind a single _connectLock semaphore so a ~200-frame reconnect storm makes each queued Task.Run publish lose the 30s race, while PublishAsync swallows all failures and FrameDetailsWrapper.cs:664 logs 'Published' unconditionally; the ThreadPool-starvation theory is refuted since socket handlers are dedicated threads and SetMinThreads(128,128) already ships.
trigger: when fleet /status freezes after a NimbusService restart while the service logs 'Published frame status'

claim: server-team's Phase 1 fix (commit bc7ce9a6, deployed 2026-07-02 12:51Z) makes the MqttHelper wedge structurally impossible by adding DisconnectSerializedAsync so the circuit-breaker's disconnect acquires _connectLock and can never overlap ConnectAsync, plus PublishAsync→Task<bool> so 'Published' is only logged on real egress; verified 0 wedge recurrences past the ~74s re-wedge mark, with publish-timeout backpressure left for Phase 2.
trigger: when checking whether the 'Not allowed to connect while connect/disconnect is pending' wedge can recur after bc7ce9a6

claim: A NimbusService restart clears the MqttHelper wedge but does NOT restore /status delivery — after each restart the broker's retained /status re-freezes once the initial ~54s burst fills the single shared publisher connection, and the only genuinely fresh fleet /status came ~2.5h after deploy when the reconnect storm fully settled — so never report 'recovered' off a post-restart burst; verify the retained newest keeps advancing toward real-time.
trigger: after a NimbusService restart — watch retained /status keep advancing over several minutes before declaring recovery

claim: Two Phase-1 verification findings on QoS0 /status: the 30s client-side publish timeout over-reports drops (bytes can egress late under backpressure), and gating the heartbeat clock on published==true makes HeartbeatDue() fire every ~10s instead of 60s under sustained timeouts — a ~6x self-inflicted heartbeat amplifier — so Phase 1.1 must advance _lastStatusPublishUtc on the attempt, not the result.
trigger: when post-deploy publish-timeout rates jump ~6x — check whether the heartbeat clock is gated on the publish result bool

claim: Correcting learning_079a7f4bef45dbb7: under single-connection send-buffer saturation the QoS0 /status 'did not egress' timeouts are genuine non-delivery (the broker's retained /status froze for 7+ minutes after the 12:51Z restart), not delivered-late, and the freeze does not self-recover in minutes — only ~2.5h of storm-settle produced fresh fleet /status — while the heartbeat-amplifier finding stands, making Phase 2 (coalescing/pooled publish) the dominant need.
trigger: when interpreting QoS0 'did not egress' counts during a saturated post-restart window — treat them as real non-delivery

claim: Frame 617's missed 07:55 scheduled wake is a frame-side standby/wake state-machine fault (suspected but unproven: an out-of-window 05:48 MQTT wake plus failing shutdowns wedged checkOnOffTimes), distinct from the resolved crop-404/collection issues; on Meural firmware 2.3.2 the bl_power verification read is chronically null but survivable, and MQTT Set powerMode=true wakes the frame when the JVM believes power is off.

when MeuralStandbyWatch logs 'rtcReadFile bl_power returned null' on firmware 2.3.2 — treat as noise, not the fault
